catalog_citation: Wega Simeu, Abraham. 2004. Etude phonologique du pólrí. Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. iii+124 pp. (MPG PuRe Language Description Heritage item_403563, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-8024-0)
catalog_locator: Première partie ch. I 'Les tons' §I.1 Définition, p. 8 (PDF p. 16); §I.4-I.5, p. 11 (PDF p. 19); Deuxième partie ('Syntagmatique') ch. I 'La syllabe' §I.1, p. 54 (PDF p. 63)
catalog_quote: (p. 8) Le polri est une langue à ton et ici, le ton représente un certain degré d'élévation ou d'abaissement de la voix pendant l'articulation de la syllabe. Nous allons donc dresser l'inventaire des tons de cette langue avant de procéder à l'identification, à la définition et au classement des tonèmes. [...] (p. 11) Les tons H, B, BH et HB ont donc une valeur distinctive dans la langue polri; ils sont; par conséquent, des tonèmes. Nous avons ainsi inventorié quatre tonèmes dans la langue. [...] En définitive, dans la langue, nous reconnaissons quatre degrés, répartis dans deux modes dont les tons ponctuels (ton bas et ton haut) et les tons modulés (ton montant et ton descendant). [...] (p. 54) Dans la langue qui constitue notre corpus la syllabe est caractérisée par plusieurs éléments dont : - Le noyau ou sommet syllabique qui est toujours une voyelle portant un ton.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: Polri is a tone language, and here tone represents a certain degree of raising or lowering of the voice during the articulation of the syllable. [...] The tones H, L, LH and HL thus have distinctive value in Polri; they are therefore tonemes. We have thus inventoried four tonemes in the language. [...] In the language of our corpus the syllable is characterised by several elements, including: the nucleus or syllable peak, which is always a vowel bearing a tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Pol is analysed as a tone language with four tonemes (H, L, rising, falling), every syllable nucleus bearing a tone; the description contains no statement about word stress or accent (no section, no mention).
new_statements.exceptions: none (some contour tones attributed to palatalisation/labialisation, p. 11 N.B.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described on isolated lexical items (word-level citation forms); no phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Wega Simeu 2004 describes the Pol (pólrí) of the canton Pol, East Region of Cameroon (reference dialect chosen §5.2, p. 5); the Congo-side variety (Pomo) is not separately treated. Same language as Glottolog pomo1271 / ISO pmm.

new_statements.relation_note: This is the very work behind the catalog's existing statement (Wega Simeu 2004, reading 'tone language, no stress statement'); re-reading the page images confirms that statement verbatim and adds nothing on stress. The catalog record itself (world-2026-09-17) carries an empty rule, which is the correct state for a source that never mentions stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Polri is described as a tone language with four contrastive tonemes (high, low, rising, falling; the rising and falling tones are 'modulated', the level ones 'punctual'); every syllable nucleus carries a tone. The thesis contains no section, heading, or sentence on word stress, accent, or prominence: a full-text search for accent/stress/proéminence/intensité/tonique/emphase/longueur/durée returns nothing, and the table of contents has no accent or intonation heading. Nothing can be said about stress placement from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None on stress. On tone, the author notes (p. 11, N.B.) that some modulated (contour) tones result from palatalization and labialization and are debatable; in the tone-distribution chapter the falling tone appears only once in CVC structures and only H and B appear in CVc structures (pp. 62-63).
new_statements.identity_note: Wega Simeu 2004 describes the Polri Kinda variety (p. 5, 'Choix du dialecte de référence': Polri has two dialects, polri kinda and polri asom, with 100% mutual intelligibility; the author chose polri Kinda as the reference dialect), with informants from Mambaya and Yaoundé. The author classifies Polri as Bantu A.90 (ALCAM code [462]), neighbour of Kwakum [463] and Kako [440]. Not opened (no open copy): Wega Simeu 2012 PhD and its published version Wega Simeu 2016, Grammaire descriptive du pólrì (Köppe, GA 51); the publisher's table of contents deposited at the DNB (already held by the project) lists tonal sections (1.3 'Système tonal', 2.3.1 'Distribution des tonèmes', 3.2.2 'Structure tonale des radicaux', 5.2.4 'Tonologie') and no accent/stress heading.
